summary: Answer-bank shortcuts solve all 54 easy instances, all 5 runner records, all 4 deduplicated survivors, and 5 reproduced stored questions. Package files remain unchanged.

source_analysis.skill: Use y=v(x)x to transform a homogeneous ODE, separate variables, integrate, substitute back, and select its general solution.
reasoning_steps: Distinguish the solution from four incorrect candidates.
invariants: Preserve the homogeneous equation, elementary integration workload, and five-choice radio response.
Keep prompts, answers, solutions, and domains consistent.
permitted_variations: Vary small signed coefficients and supported integration branches.
Vary distractor relationships so candidate appearance alone does not reveal correctness.

source_replay.details: All three easy sources reproduce their equations and complete answer banks. Nine implemented source cases replay mathematically; unsupported canonical and moderate families are documented.

math.details: Independent symbolic checks verify all 54 easy instances and five runner records, including uniqueness of the correct solution.

variety.details: All coefficient slots are covered, but each recognizable family preserves a perfect answer-bank shortcut. The exact batch and its survivors remain entirely answerable using those shortcuts.

scope.details: Easy variations preserve the substitution, integration techniques, workload, and response contract.

grading.details: Native grader: 186 accepted and 276 rejected checks, zero unresolved. Tests include every alternative and shortcut predictions. Free-entry equivalence is inapplicable to radio questions.

rendering.details: Actual UI rendered ten controlled instances and all four batch survivors. Representative screenshots were inspected; notation, controls, and solutions display correctly.

packaging.details: Exact Python dependency matches. Determinism, relocation, invalid-input rejection, and JSON output pass. Package hashes are unchanged.

decision_variation.details: Each conditional shortcut scores 18/18 against a 0.2 random-choice baseline. Combined rules score 49/49 after delivery filtering. Five affected stored generated questions were reproduced with matching UUIDs and content fingerprints.

findings.description: The answer banks reveal correctness without reading the ODE: choose the unique cube-root candidate; for linear-log banks, choose the sole candidate containing both x ln|x| and +Cx; for affine banks, choose the smaller absolute linear coefficient among the two Cx^2 candidates. These rules solve the entire easy domain and supplied batch. UI shuffling preserves these cues.

findings.reproduction: Run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/.venv/bin/python reproduce_shortcut.py from evidence_root; it exits 1. Minimal case: generate('cube_root', 2, seed=826033), retained in minimal-failing-record.json. For y'=(2x^3+y^3)/(xy^2), selecting the sole cube-root candidate yields the accepted answer without determining the integration coefficient. Changing a to -2 preserves the same successful shortcut.
findings.requested_change: Change extension-bank construction so candidate shapes and fixed coefficient comparisons cannot identify correctness. Use plausible same-shape distractors requiring the surviving term and integration coefficient to be calculated; vary affine distractor magnitudes. Preserve source replay and difficulty, regenerate the batch, and retain the strict shortcut regression.
